newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures open lower after Tankan slams dlr.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures open lower after Tankan slams dlr.

text.p: U.S. debt futures opened lower Wednesday on residual weakness stemming from an overnight dive in dollar/yen on a strong Japan Tankan business survey.

Traders said the dollar's plunge overnight weighed on Treasury prices and placed technical pressure on bond futures, which in turn brought in hedge selling before the five-year note auction set for midday.

However, they said volume in futures was light at the opening, as it has been throughout the week so far, and several traders predicted prices would remain well-supported, with buying interest readily apparent on the early dips.
"The market seems to be stable at these lower levels," said Donald Pullen, bond floor analyst with ED&F Man.

Pullen said market participants remain optimistic about the bond market overall based on the fundamentals, with the Federal Open Market Committee expected to remain on the sidelines at next week's two-day meeting.
Those with long positions acquired during the upswing of the past two months appear comfortable holding onto those positions as they eye price objectives that have yet to be met, Pullen added.
This morning, the U.S. Commerce Department reported durable goods orders in May fell 0.6 percent, compared with market expectations for a 0.6 percent rise.
The market is awaiting data on May U.S. existing home sales at 0900 CDT, projected to have risen to 4.07 million units from 4.06 million previously.
At midday, the Treasury will auction $11.5 billion in five-year notes.
Traders said they expected futures activity to remain light awaiting the auction results, with prices likely to continue to hover above the session lows.

Overnight, the dollar shed 1.5 yen on a strong improvement in business sentiment shown in the Bank of Japan's quarterly Tankan survey, fueling talk of a rate hike in that nation. However, it recovered some ground and was trading around 113.90 yen.
Support for September bond futures was seen at 111-17, a double bottom from last week, with resistance at the overnight high of 112-07.

September bonds were 12/32 lower at 111-25/32, December Eurodollars were down 0.015 points at 93.925, and September 10-year note futures were 7/32 lower at 108-10/32. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
